points.t: Itchy wheals that come and go within a day, with or without lip/eyelid swelling — skin looks normal between attacks.
Mast-cell histamine (and other mediators) → dermal oedema (wheal) and deeper oedema (angioedema). Most CSU is autoimmune/idiopathic, not a hidden food allergy.
Daily second-generation H1 antihistamine; up-dose up to 4× licensed dose if needed; short steroid only for severe acute flares; refer uncontrolled CSU for omalizumab pathways.
Anaphylaxis (ABC) → adrenaline/999. ACE-inhibitor angioedema without wheals — stop the ACEI urgently. Lesions lasting >24 h with bruising → urticarial vasculitis.

points: Mast-cell degranulation (IgE, autoimmune, idiopathic, or direct — NSAIDs, opioids, contrast).
CSU is usually not an IgE food allergy — restrictive diets and patch tests do not help.
ACE inhibitors cause bradykinin angioedema that can start months to years after initiation.
Inducible triggers: dermographism, delayed pressure, cholinergic, cold, solar, aquagenic.
Wheals: itchy, pink or skin-coloured, migrate, **individually fade within 24 hours**, leave normal skin.
In skin of colour, feel for oedema when erythema is subtle.
Angioedema: lips, eyelids, hands, genitals — may burn more than itch.
Vasculitis clue: lesions >24 h, burning/pain, purpura or residual bruise.
Clinical history ± phone photos. Acute urticaria: **no routine tests**.
CSU: keep tests minimal — FBC and CRP/ESR reasonable; thyroid tests only if indicated. **Patch testing has no role** in urticaria.
Activity tools: UAS7 / UCT for severity and omalizumab eligibility discussions.
Suspected inducible disease: challenge testing in clinic/specialist settings.

items.t: Lesions lasting >24 h with purpura → vasculitis work-up.
Fever, arthralgia, weight loss with urticarial rash → systemic disease / Schnitzler consideration.
CSU uncontrolled on up-dosed antihistamine → refer.

pearls.t: “It isn’t an allergy to something you keep eating” — most CSU is internal.
Take the antihistamine every day, even on good days; step down slowly once controlled.
Patch testing investigates eczema, not wheals.
Always check BNF for residual renal/hepatic dosing and pregnancy.
Swelling without wheals on an ACE inhibitor: see [ACE-inhibitor angioedema](condition:ace-inhibitor-angioedema).
Wheals lasting more than 24 hours that bruise or burn: see [urticarial vasculitis](condition:urticarial-vasculitis).
